fatal_errors: The proposed continuous-B2 baseline microstructure is not established for HfZrTiTa0.53; it is transferred from the compositionally distinct Al0.5NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr alloy in E2.
The intervention does not reconstruct the supported Ta-Nb-V alloying strategy or the HfZrTi(TaNbV)x compositional series.

The reported 13.5% terminal strain is treated as tensile elongation and even as uniform elongation, although the cited baseline is a compressive result and does not establish tensile uniform elongation.

Impact-triggered energy release of HfZrTiTa0.53 is asserted without direct cited evidence; the thin-steel penetration evidence concerns WFeNiMo fragments, while E2 reports mechanical behavior of another alloy.
The mechanism and falsification experiment omit verification that B2-to-BCC phase inversion actually occurs in HfZrTiTa0.53.
explanation: The response addresses the broad engineering objective and proposes a controlled comparison with tensile, compression, and impact tests, but its central material premise is unsupported. E2 demonstrates phase inversion and improved compressive ductility in a different Al-Nb-Ta-Ti-V-Zr alloy; it does not show that HfZrTiTa0.53 contains a continuous ordered B2 matrix or will respond similarly to annealing. E1 only supports the general warning that compression can conceal severe tensile brittleness. In contrast, the target intervention is systematic 1:1:1 Ta-Nb-V addition to as-cast HfZrTi, producing HfZrTi(TaNbV)x and stabilizing BCC while suppressing HCP and omega phases at sufficient x. The target also requires the approximately 4000 s^-1 SHPB-in-air energy-release regime, fragmentation-driven oxidation, and the observed HZTX0.9 tensile properties. The proposed experiment is partly discriminating, but it needs phase characterization, explicit uniform-elongation measurement, controlled dynamic compression near 4000 s^-1 in air, and quantitative ignition/luminosity criteria. Its numerical ductility target is based on misclassifying terminal compressive strain as baseline tensile elongation.
